title: Honey Garlic Chicken Rice Bowls
seoTitle: Honey Garlic Chicken Rice Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Skillet glazed chicken thighs over jasmine rice with steamed broccoli
subtitle: Skillet glazed chicken thighs over jasmine rice with steamed broccoli
description: Boneless chicken thighs sear in a honey-garlic-soy glaze, then serve over fluffy jasmine rice with steamed broccoli and sesame seeds.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Honey Garlic Chicken Rice Bowls in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Cook rice and steam broccoli
steps.instruction: Cook jasmine rice per package directions. Steam broccoli 4–5 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp, not olive drab or mushy.

steps.title: Sear chicken thighs
steps.instruction: Heat 1 tbsp oil in two skillets over medium-high. Sear thighs 4–5 minutes per side until golden and internal temp reaches 165°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Prepare honey garlic glaze
steps.instruction: Whisk soy sauce, honey, vinegar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and cornstarch until smooth with no starch lumps at the bottom. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Glaze chicken in pan
steps.instruction: Pour glaze over seared thighs. Simmer 3–4 minutes, turning often, until sauce thickens to a glossy coat that clings to the meat. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Build bowls at the line
steps.instruction: Slice chicken and portion over rice with broccoli. Drizzle extra glaze, top with green onion and sesame seeds. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

proTips: Do not crowd the pan—searing in batches keeps the glaze from turning soupy.
Use low-sodium soy so the honey sweetness does not taste cloying.
Offer sriracha at the line for heat without changing the base recipe.
tonightSpread: Quick miso soup cups for a light starter.
Cucumber salad with rice vinegar and sesame.
leftovers: Pack rice and chicken together; refresh with microwave and extra soy-honey drizzle.
Shred chicken into fried rice next shift with frozen peas and carrots.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Takeout-style bowls with less sodium and more protein. A build-your-own line keeps service fast when everyone hits the kitchen at once.
mealPrepNotes: Cook rice in a rice cooker while chicken sears. Mix glaze in a jar and shake before adding to the pan. Station: Set up bowl line: rice base, chicken, broccoli, sauce drizzle, sesame and green onion. Station: Keep glaze warm in a squeeze bottle for portion control and consistent sweetness. Station: Use two skillets so all thighs finish searing at the same time.
